stories.title: India Extends AFSPA in Parts of Manipur, Nagaland, and Arunachal
stories.what_happened: The Ministry of Home Affairs extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act in parts of Manipur, Nagaland, and Arunachal Pradesh for six months following a law and order review. The decision applies to designated districts and police station areas across the three states.
stories.impact: The act grants deployed armed forces powers to search, arrest without warrants, and use lethal force, alongside immunity from prosecution without central sanction.
stories.whats_next: The extension takes effect on October 1, 2026, and will remain in force until March 31, 2027, unless withdrawn earlier.

stories.title: Centre Appoints Mandeep K. Bhandari as New CBSE Chairperson
stories.what_happened: On September 25, 2026, the Centre appointed senior IAS officer Mandeep K. Bhandari as chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education. Hindustan Times reported that Bhandari is the third officer to head the board in under four months. His appointment follows the June 2 removal of former chairperson Rahul Singh.
stories.impact: The leadership shift follows a one-member government inquiry into the procurement of the board's On-Screen Marking digital evaluation system.

stories.title: Protests and Legal Actions Target CEC Gyanesh Kumar Over Electoral Revision
stories.what_happened: Opposition parties staged nationwide protests demanding the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. According to Hindustan Times, Congress protested in Delhi and at least 11 states, where police used water cannons and detained leaders. Supreme Court advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi filed a petition seeking Kumar's criminal prosecution.
stories.impact: NDA allies, including Union Minister Chirag Paswan and Upendra Kushwaha, publicly demanded that the Election Commission clarify its stance on the revision process.
stories.whats_next: Cockroach Janata Party announced it will launch a nationwide protest from Mumbai starting October 2 if Gyanesh Kumar does not resign.

stories.title: Uttarakhand Issued Heavy Rain Alerts as Authorities Go on High Alert
stories.what_happened: The India Meteorological Department issued red, orange, and yellow rain alerts for multiple Uttarakhand districts in late September. Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed departments to maintain high vigilance and prepare relief arrangements. According to The Times of India, Secretary of Disaster Management Vinod Kumar Suman instructed all 13 districts to remain on alert.
stories.impact: Authorities advised pilgrims, tourists, and the public to avoid non-essential travel and landslide-prone areas. According to Hindustan Times, more than 33 roads were already blocked across Uttarakhand.
stories.whats_next: Heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms is expected to continue through September 28 as local authorities monitor rising water levels and clear blocked roads.

stories.title: NDA Allies Urge Election Commission to Clarify Electoral Revision Doubts
stories.what_happened: Three NDA allies—LJP (Ram Vilas), Rashtriya Lok Morcha, and the Telugu Desam Party—have urged the Election Commission of India to issue a clarification to dispel public confusion. The request follows reports of internal dissent over the electoral revision process. The Election Commission refuted the report, stating all final decisions are made unanimously.
stories.impact: Party leaders stated that transparency and an official clarification from the Election Commission are necessary to preserve public trust and confidence in the electoral process.

evidence.headline: Centre extends AFSPA in Manipur, Nagaland, and Arunachal Pradesh for six months

published_claims.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs extended the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 in parts of Manipur, Arunachal Pradesh, and Nagaland for six months.
The extension of AFSPA is effective from October 1, 2026.
The extension will remain in force until March 31, 2027, unless withdrawn earlier.
In Arunachal Pradesh, AFSPA was extended in Tirap, Changlang, and Longding districts, as well as areas under Namsai, Mahadevpur, and Chowkham police stations in Namsai district.

evidence.headline: Govt appoints Mandeep Bhandari as CBSE chairperson amid evaluation controversy

published_claims.text: The Centre appointed senior IAS officer Mandeep K. Bhandari as the chairperson of the Central Board of Secondary Education.
Bhandari's appointment order was issued on September 25, 2026.
Bhandari is a 2001-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre.
Bhandari is the third officer to head CBSE in less than four months.
Before this appointment, Bhandari served as principal secretary to the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir since March 6, 2023.
On June 2, the government removed former CBSE chairperson Rahul Singh and secretary Himanshu Gupta following the OSM controversy.
The government ordered a one-member inquiry headed by former Union secretary S. Radha Chauhan into the procurement of the OSM digital evaluation system.
Bhandari holds a medical degree (MBBS).

evidence.headline: Opposition protests, NDA allies seek answers as pressure mounts on ECI

published_claims.text: Congress and other opposition parties staged protests across India demanding the removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Congress staged protests in Delhi and at least 11 states and union territories, where police used water cannons and detained several senior leaders.
Police detained senior Congress leaders, including Assam Congress chief Gaurav Gogoi, during protests.
Police fired water cannons on protesting Congress workers in Patna and Chandigarh.

An Indian Express investigation reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded written dissents and objections at least 14 times between November 2025 and August 2026.
Union Minister and Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan publicly called on CEC Gyanesh Kumar to clearly present the ECI's stance to the public.
Rashtriya Lok Manch chief Upendra Kushwaha asked the Election Commission to immediately issue a clarification on the controversy surrounding the SIR.
The opposition previously submitted two impeachment notices against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on March 12 and April 24.
Supreme Court advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking criminal prosecution of CEC Gyanesh Kumar for alleged unilateral and unauthorised decisions.
Advocate Shiv Kumar Tripathi wrote to the Attorney General seeking consent to initiate contempt proceedings against Gyanesh Kumar.
The petition in the Supreme Court seeks quashing of modifications made to Form 6 on ECINet and ERONet portals that require ancestry and last-SIR declarations.
Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray called for the complete scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision process and a return to ballot papers.
Raj Thackeray made his statement and Congress protests occurred on September 25, 2026.

evidence.headline: IMD issues red and orange alerts for severe rainfall in Uttarakhand; CM orders high vigilance

published_claims.text: The IMD issued red and orange rain alerts for multiple districts in Uttarakhand.
For Saturday, September 26, five districts are placed under a red alert: Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital, and Udham Singh Nagar.
For Saturday, September 26, five districts are placed under an orange alert: Dehradun, Pauri (Pauri Garhwal), Rudraprayag, Chamoli, and Almora.
Three districts are under a yellow alert for September 26: Haridwar, Uttarkashi, and Tehri (Tehri Garhwal).
For Sunday, September 27, an orange alert has been issued for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital, and Rudraprayag.
Five districts are under a yellow alert on Sunday, September 27: Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar, and Pithoragarh.
Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed officials and concerned departments to maintain high vigilance and keep relief and rescue arrangements ready.
Officials and authorities advised pilgrims, tourists, and the public to avoid non-essential travel and avoid rivers, streams, and landslide-prone areas.
Secretary of Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.
Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman to review weather preparedness.
Emergency operation centre contact numbers were provided: 1070 for the State Emergency Operation Centre, 1077 for the District Emergency Operation Centre, and 112 for emergency services.
High-altitude areas at and above 4,000 metres are likely to receive snowfall between September 25 and 28.
More than 33 roads were blocked across Uttarakhand, including 14 in Chamoli and 10 in Dehradun.
Uttarakhand recorded 0.5 mm of rainfall against a normal of 4.6 mm in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 am on Friday, an 89% shortfall.
Helicopter operations to Kedarnath Dham would be suspended as a precaution if adverse weather conditions impact flying.

evidence.headline: NDA allies ask Election Commission to clarify stand amid dissent row

published_claims.text: Three NDA allies asked the Election Commission of India to issue a clarification to dispel public doubts over the electoral revision process and reported internal dissent.
An investigative report stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded objections to decisions at least 14 times over 10 months.
Union Minister Chirag Paswan called on the Election Commission to forcefully clarify its stance to assure the public and preserve trust in the electoral process.
Upendra Kushwaha of the Rashtriya Lok Morcha urged the Election Commission to immediately issue a clarification to clear up confusion among the public regarding the SIR exercise.
TDP Lok Sabha floor leader Lavu Srikrishna Devarayalu stated that providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency would help strengthen public confidence in the ECI.
The Election Commission refuted the report, stating that internal checks and balances are standard practice and that all final decisions are taken unanimously.
Rahul Gandhi called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following the report.
Arvind Kejriwal demanded the arrest and prosecution of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and called for recent elections in Delhi, Bihar, West Bengal, and Maharashtra to be re-held.
More than 10 crore voters' names are reported to have been struck off electoral rolls under the SIR exercise.
BJP West Bengal unit chief Samik Bhattacharya suggested Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar be awarded the Padma Bhushan.
Gyanesh Kumar became an Election Commissioner in 2024 and Chief Election Commissioner in 2025.

evidence.what_happened: Three NDA allies—LJP (Ram Vilas), Rashtriya Lok Morcha, and the Telugu Desam Party—urged the Election Commission of India to issue a clear clarification to dispel public confusion after reports surfaced regarding internal differences over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
